quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Driving at night using only parking lights is against the law.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: You cannot drive at night using only parking lights. You must use your headlights when driving in the dark.

questions.question: Highway signs that show hazardous conditions are called:

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning signs.
questions.explanation: Warning signs tell drivers about dangerous conditions ahead. You must follow warning signs for your safety. Not obeying them could cause an accident.

questions.question: A single broken white line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A broken line means you can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: A steady yellow light at an intersection means:

options.text: Go.
Yield to other cars.
Slow down and prepare to stop.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and prepare to stop.
questions.explanation: A yellow light warns that a red light is coming next. Slow down and prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, continue through with care.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is approaching you on a one-way street. You must:

options.text: Turn on your flashers and drive.
Move to the nearest side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until it passes you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the nearest side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches on a one-way street, move to the nearest side of the road and stop.

questions.question: Your blind spot is the area you:

options.text: Cannot see without turning your head.
See directly behind your vehicle.
See in your rearview mirror.
See in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see without turning your head. They are found to the sides of and behind your vehicle.

questions.question: The space you need to cross traffic depends on:

options.text: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
Whether there is a stop sign.
Using your turn signals.
Cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on the road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: A bicyclist who breaks traffic laws:

options.text: Does not have to follow traffic laws.
Can be ticketed.
Will always get a warning from police.
Will have their bicycle taken away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be ticketed.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as car drivers. Both can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT help with safe night driving?

options.text: Keep your windshield clean.
Know that tinted windows reduce visibility at night.
Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.
Look directly into oncoming headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look directly into oncoming headlights.
questions.explanation: Looking into oncoming headlights makes your pupils contract. After the car passes, your eyes need time to readjust. During this time, you cannot see well.

questions.question: The correct order of traffic lights from top to bottom is:

options.text: Red, yellow, green.
Red, green, yellow.
Green, red, yellow.
Green, yellow, red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Red, yellow, green.
questions.explanation: Red is always on top and green is always on bottom for vertical lights. Red is always on the left and green is always on the right for horizontal lights.

questions.question: When two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
Drivers must use hand signals to communicate with each other.
One driver should go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles go in the order they arrive. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
No U-turn.
Yield.
Do not enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter.
questions.explanation: This sign is placed at the start of one-way streets and ramps. It tells you that you cannot continue driving in your current direction.

questions.question: Your stereo volume should not be so loud that you cannot hear traffic sounds.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Set your stereo volume before you drive. If you cannot hear traffic sounds over your stereo, turn down the volume.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A steep hill is coming.
You must turn left ahead.
Do not enter.
A four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A four-way intersection is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots?

options.text: By looking in your side mirrors.
By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
By looking in your rearview mirror.
By looking straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Check them by turning your head and looking over your shoulders.

questions.question: What can help you avoid making emergency stops in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to let others know you are there.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from the car in front of you.
Drive in the right lane only.
Drive slower than other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance lets you react to problems ahead without an emergency stop. An emergency stop could cause the driver behind you to crash into you.

questions.question: On a freeway, you miss your exit. What should you do?

options.text: Make the turn quickly from your lane.
Stop and back up.
Continue to the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue to the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, continue to the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around. Never back up on a freeway or shoulder—it is illegal.

questions.question: When you want to turn right, where should your car be?

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection when you begin to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Before turning right, move as far to the right side of the road as possible. Do not cut across other lanes to make any turn.

questions.question: Can you cross a double solid yellow line to pass another car?

options.text: Yes.
No.
Yes, if there is no oncoming traffic.
Yes, if the car ahead is going under the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: No.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing. You cannot cross them unless you are turning into a driveway or business entrance. No passing is allowed over a solid yellow line.

questions.question: If you stop along the road at night, what lights should you use?

options.text: Turn off all your lights.
Use your parking lights only.
Use your headlights only.
Turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beams on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beams on.
questions.explanation: If you stop along the road at night, turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beam headlights on. This makes sure other drivers can see your vehicle clearly.

questions.question: You can reduce the risk of hydroplaning by driving:

options.text: Through shallow water.
Faster.
Slower.
Through deep water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slower.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast in wet conditions. Driving slower reduces the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: If the road ahead is covered with water, you should:

options.text: Drive until you think the water is too deep.
Drive through, because the water is unlikely to get deeper.
Turn around and take a different route.
Walk into the water to check how deep it is.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn around and take a different route.
questions.explanation: If a road is flooded, turn around and find another way. Never drive through flood water. You cannot tell how deep it is or how strong the current is. Your vehicle could be swept away or sink.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Keep the same speed.
Slow down to give them room to pass safely and quickly.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give them room to pass safely and quickly.
questions.explanation: When a driver behind you wants to pass, slow down. This creates space in front of your vehicle so they can complete the pass safely and in less time.

questions.question: Your speed does not affect how far your vehicle travels after you brake.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: FALSE
questions.explanation: Speed matters a lot when braking. The faster you drive, the longer the distance needed to stop. Stay far behind other vehicles, especially at high speeds.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, you should:

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the road.
Stop your car at the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: If your wheels go off the pavement, reduce your speed without braking hard. Turn carefully back onto the road. Watch for other traffic before re-entering.

questions.question: Distracted driving can be caused by:

options.text: Eating, drinking, or smoking.
Talking or texting on a phone.
Changing the radio station or CD.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Drivers make about 200 decisions for every mile driven. You must focus on driving. Any other activity creates a dangerous distraction.

questions.question: If your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement, you should:

options.text: Stop quickly.
Immediately pull all the way off the road and get back on when it is safe.
Speed up and steer back onto the road quickly.
Release the accelerator, slow down, then carefully steer back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator, slow down, then carefully steer back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: If your right wheels leave the pavement, stay calm. Release the accelerator and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and ease back onto the road with a small turn of the wheel. Use both hands and check for traffic.

questions.question: Defensive driving means:

options.text: Recognizing dangerous situations and acting to prevent accidents.
Competing with poor drivers by passing them in traffic.
Staying close behind other vehicles.
Quickly changing lanes to move through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Recognizing dangerous situations and acting to prevent accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means spotting dangerous situations and taking action before an accident happens. It helps you avoid crashes caused by aggressive, careless, or impaired drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: You must stop for a school bus:

options.text: That is parked on the shoulder with no one in it.
When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.
On a two-lane highway when its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a two-lane highway when its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop when a school bus displays flashing red lights while picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop as long as the red lights are flashing or the stop arm is out.

questions.question: When passing a large vehicle in a small vehicle, be prepared for:

options.text: Loud noises.
Excess air pollution.
Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.
Falling vehicle parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create strong wind gusts that can push smaller vehicles off course. Be ready to steer correctly when passing or approaching large vehicles at highway speeds.

questions.question: Before turning, you should:

options.text: Use your signal.
Turn the wheel.
Increase your speed.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your signal.
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn. This tells other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended, you must:

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
Honk your horn before passing the bus on its left.
Continue driving when you think most children are done leaving the bus.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has its stop arm out, you must stop completely. Do not move until the stop arm is pulled in.

questions.question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road:

options.text: Has the right-of-way.
Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume that other drivers will change lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: When you enter a public road from a driveway or private road, you must let drivers already on the road go first. Merge safely when it is clear.

questions.question: When you see flashing signals at a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the vehicle ahead of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: Stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail when you see flashing signals or lowered gates. Also watch for moving trains. Never try to cross in front of a train.

questions.question: At a school crossing sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop, whether there's a stop sign or not.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always sound your horn when you see children.
Be ready to help children crossing the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Always watch for pedestrians at crossings and be prepared to stop. Let pedestrians cross safely.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at the same time at a four-way stop sign intersection:

options.text: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
One driver may continue driving without stopping.
One driver should honk to indicate that they are giving up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, if you arrive at the same time as another driver, let the driver on your right go first. You can then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: A seat belt should fit:

options.text: Loosely.
Snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Hidden beneath the seat.
Loose enough to silence the seat belt warning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower belly. The shoulder belt should fit comfortably so you can fit your fist between it and your chest.

questions.question: When it starts to rain while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Drive faster than the traffic around you.
Drive at the maximum posted speed limit.
Slow down.
Drive closely behind the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When rain reduces visibility, reduce your speed. Turn on your headlights so others can see you. If rain is very heavy and you cannot see, pull over and stop until it clears.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: There is a detour ahead.
You must stop for flaggers.
The road ahead is closed to traffic.
The highway ahead is undergoing maintenance.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highway ahead is undergoing maintenance.
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn drivers about construction and maintenance work ahead. Slow down and drive carefully when you see these signs.

questions.question: Crossbuck signs tell drivers about:

options.text: Railroad crossings.
School zones.
No passing zones.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs mark railroad crossings. Yield to trains at these crossings. Never try to race a train across the tracks.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing without flashing lights or gates, you should:

options.text: Cross the tracks right away as fast as possible.
Always stop before crossing the tracks.
Be ready to let any train pass first.
Speed up to cross before a train arrives.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to let any train pass first.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to let any oncoming trains pass before crossing railroad tracks. This is especially important if there are no lights or gates at the crossing. Do not cross until your entire vehicle can fit on the other side. Do not change gears while crossing because your vehicle might stall.

questions.question: This sign indicates that:

options.text: A steep hill is ahead.
Trucks are not allowed on the upcoming hill.
A logging road is ahead.
Trucks are on the upcoming hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill or downgrade is coming.

questions.question: To be ready for anything on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Look at the entire road and both sides constantly.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Keep your eyes on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and both sides constantly.
questions.explanation: Your ability to handle dangerous situations depends on spotting problems early. Looking far ahead does not mean staring only at the center of the road. You need to scan the entire road and both sides.

questions.question: When driving near children playing, you should expect them to:

options.text: Know when it is safe to cross the street.
Stop at the curb before crossing the street.
Run in front of you without looking.
Not cross the street unless an adult is with them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Run in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and be extra careful when children are nearby. They may not understand danger and could run in front of your car without looking.

questions.question: You are in the right lane of a multilane highway and want to move to the left lane. You should:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you before changing lanes.
Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Check your side mirror and turn on your signal.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure no vehicles are in the lane you want to enter. Always use your signal when changing lanes.

questions.question: Night driving requires extra caution because:

options.text: Traffic moves faster at night.
There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.
More accidents happen at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: Darkness makes it hard for drivers to see. From 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise, or anytime vehicles are not visible for 500 feet, you must use your headlights.

questions.question: A railroad crossbuck sign should be treated the same as a yield sign.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: A railroad crossbuck sign is a yield sign. You must let any trains and railroad equipment pass first.

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic light means a ____ light will appear soon.

options.text: Flashing yellow
Steady green
Steady red
Flashing red

questions.correctAnswerText: Steady red
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light warns you that a steady red light is coming next.

questions.question: You may park in the access aisles next to handicap parking spaces.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Do not park in handicap access aisles. These spaces are needed for wheelchairs and wheelchair lifts.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) depends on everything except:

options.text: Your body weight.
How much you drink.
How much time passes between drinks.
How physically fit you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: How physically fit you are.
questions.explanation: Your BAC depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Your fitness level does not affect your BAC.
